Where does the Kuberostics skeleton stand?

Long image

A

Answer

The motion skeleton of spec 001 is built, reviewed and tested: a supervisor, a latched stop lock that the real twist_mux honors, and three stubs. What is missing is the launch file, the contract tests and every run that needs CoppeliaSim.

  1. The stop lock works with the real twist_mux on Jazzy and Lyrical, checked by a Docker probe.1
  2. All logic sits in pure-Python cores with thin LifecycleNodes, so 86 tests run without ROS graphs or a simulator.
  3. The reviewer agent approved the supervisor, stop_guard and the stubs after at most two rounds.
  4. Nothing has run against the simulator yet: headless CoppeliaSim crashes on the Kinect render.

Applies toSpec 001 at commit c352b2c. Tests run in Docker, not on the robot.

  • behaviour_server behaviour
  • stuck_detector stuck

  • Wheel bridge bridge

  • escape → mux · mux/escape

  1. supervisor ↗

    Turns the IA368II mode and stuck events into submodes and owns the stop lock.

  2. coverage_server ↗

    Publishes a constant Twist on its own mux input while a goal is active.

  3. escape_server ↗

    Runs a scripted reverse-and-turn and answers with a result.

  4. twist_mux ↗

    The only node that publishes /myRobot/cmd_vel.

What happens when the robot gets stuck?

Diagram structure
  • stuck_detector stuck
  • supervisor sup
  • escape_server esc
  • coverage_server cov
  • stop_guard guard
  • twist_mux mux
  • stuck → sup · StuckEvent
  • sup → esc · Escape
  • esc → mux · Twist
  • esc → sup · success
  • sup → cov · resume
  • sup → guard · lock_stop = true
  • guard → mux · zero Twist
3

Why does stop_guard exist?

twist_mux publishes nothing while a lock is active, so a plain lock leaves the last command alive downstream. stop_guard feeds a zero Twist into an input that outranks the lock.2

Mux inputTopicPriorityFed by
stop {good:Highest}/myRobot/mux/stop250stop_guard, only while locked
lock/myRobot/mux/lock_stop200supervisor
teleop/myRobot/mux/teleop100keyboard teleop
escape/myRobot/mux/escape80escape_server
coverage/myRobot/mux/coverage50coverage_server
docking/myRobot/mux/docking40later spec

Known limit

If the supervisor process restarts while locked, the lock is released. The lock survives lifecycle cycles but not a process restart.

4

Which supervisor rules are implemented?

RequirementBehaviour
R19stop_guard publishes zero at 10 Hz or more, only while locked.
R20Priority order is stop, then lock, then drivers. The stop input times out in 0.5 s.
R21AUTODOCKING while COVERING cancels coverage. A mode change during ESCAPING updates the resume target.
R22The lock is independent of the submode. Only /myRobot/supervisor/reset releases it.

The pure state machine holds these rules, so each one has a plain pytest case.3

5

What is tested?

45 + 22 + 11 + 8 = 86 tests. vacuum_interfaces holds only messages and actions, so it has none.

Open decisions

Constitution Art. VI.2 still says the stop lock has maximum priority, but D-22 puts the stop input at 250 above the lock at 200. Does the 2025S2 wheel bridge have its own command timeout? Check with Q-01. Q-05 and Q-06 are unresolved.
